ensures: route_capabilities is total over ordinary values and returns one closed immutable CapabilityRouteResult with status routed, unsupported, ambiguous, invalid, or exhausted; no ordinary failure returns a partial registry, candidate set, selection, executable handle, or mathematical authority.

Before routing, the function independently validates every complete TheoryPlugin descriptor, replays the exact session event chain, proves the named head/context/normalization/obligation current, parses the accepted canonical-normalization bytes, and derives every fragment dimension from those bytes.

Registration binds descriptor content, plugin ID/version, implementation, producer/checker, contracts, schemas, capabilities, formats, cost models, operations, lifecycle, effects, replay, dependencies, platforms, extensions, and limits without importing an entry point or executing plugin code.

Byte-identical descriptors are idempotent; nonidentical logical plugin-version, component, capability, namespace, format, or dependency identities collide fail-closed for the entire registry independently of descriptor order.

Required dependencies resolve to one exact descriptor hash and compatible semantic-version interval inside the registry, form an acyclic graph, and are explicitly available; names, optional declarations, host discovery, or compatible-looking versions never substitute.

Eligibility is exact containment across theory, domain, quantifier, expression, relation, polynomial degree, quantifier count/depth, variable and node counts, goals, ambiguity, arithmetic, theory features, operation, Evidence and Certificate formats, contracts, schemas, platform, effects, replay, lifecycle, availability, and dependency closure.
Every capability is projected exactly once as an eligible candidate or an incompatibility with complete closed dimension-level reason codes; no capability disappears because another wins.

Cost is the exact portable-integer sum of the descriptor base, per-variable, per-expression-node, per-quantifier-count, per-goal, and ambiguity terms, saturates at the declared maximum, and retains all terms in the derivation.

Eligible candidates order by cost ascending, priority descending, capability ID, plugin ID, and parsed semantic version ascending. Routed selects the unique first candidate; unresolved upstream reading choice or a non-unique exact rank is ambiguous and selects none.

Candidates bind exact descriptor, capability, operation, component, session, revision, context, normalization, obligation, derived fragment, availability, dependency, format, effect, replay, cost, and route identities and always carry mathematical_authority false.

Unsupported returns a complete valid registry, derived fragment, and incompatibilities but no candidates or selection; invalid and exhausted return no registry, fragment, candidates, incompatibilities, selection, result digest, or authority.

Changing any descriptor, artifact, session, revision, context, reading, obligation, availability, platform, effect, operation, format, replay, dependency, cost, priority, budget, schema, or contract changes or invalidates the route identity and cannot reuse a prior result.

Keyword, substring, regex, edit distance, display name, description, prose, embedding, model output, profile label, popularity, catalogue/import order, clock, randomness, paths, object identity, repr, and host state never affect registry, eligibility, cost, ordering, or identity.

All public registry values are closed final immutable exact dataclasses or tuples; direct construction, subclassing, mutation, alias mutation, object.__new__ forgery, dataclass replacement, pickling, noncanonical parsing, and repaired outer hashes cannot create a valid route.
MemoryError, KeyboardInterrupt, and SystemExit propagate unchanged and can never become routed, selected, supported, completed, producer-reported, checker-attested, or externally verified.

epistemics.ambiguous: the exact current reading or selection is non-unique and no capability is selected
epistemics.authority: mathematical_authority is always false; later governed producers and independent checkers alone may create Evidence or Certificate authority
epistemics.candidate: registration, support, low cost, lifecycle readiness, or ranking never implies truth, solvability, execution success, Evidence validity, or checker attestation
epistemics.exhausted: deterministic work ended before any partial state escaped
epistemics.incompatibility: one supplied structural mismatch explains exclusion only
epistemics.invalid: input, artifact, descriptor, dependency, registry, context, canonicalization, identity, or result validation failed with no partial state
epistemics.routed: one exact compatible candidate is selected for later planning; this is structural eligibility only
epistemics.unsupported: no registered capability satisfies every request dimension; this makes no mathematical impossibility claim

invariants: The eight accepted schema identities are compiled into production and rebound independently before request, descriptor, artifact, registry, or result use.

A registry is the canonical content-sorted set of complete descriptor entries and dependency closure, containing no module, callable, object reference, entry point, open file, process handle, secret, machine path, environment value, or host claim.
Plugin ID/version is unique unless descriptor bytes are identical; component IDs, capability IDs, namespace ownership, and advertised format identities cannot collide across nonidentical descriptors.

Each descriptor satisfies the complete accepted TheoryPlugin contract and cannot weaken distinct producer/checker, compatibility, lifecycle, effect, replay, budget, Evidence, Certificate, provenance, or authority rules.
Every required dependency resolves by exact descriptor hash and compatible version inside one acyclic registry and explicit availability closure.
The request binds one capability kind/operation pair, exact format needs, explicit platform/availability/effect/replay policy, current session head/context, and current canonical obligation.

Session replay proves the named normalization artifact, reading, obligation and context current; cross-session, cross-reading, retired, superseded, invalidated, missing, or hash-similar records never route.
Fragment derivation is a complete deterministic projection of the exact canonical obligation/context and includes every TheoryPlugin routing dimension; caller or plugin labels cannot override it.
Eligibility requires complete containment and exact compatibility; absent, unknown, ambiguous, unavailable, or over-limit dimensions fail closed and are never wildcarded.
Cost coefficients/counts/products/sums are nonnegative portable integers; overflow fails, saturation is explicit, and low cost never repairs ineligibility.
Candidate and incompatibility projections are complete, deterministic and disjoint; all nested and aggregate identities are recomputed by strict validation.
No result implies truth, consistency, proof, refutation, witness validity, checker freshness, plugin honesty, actual host availability, or successful future execution.
Legacy recommend_tool text, MCP descriptions, profile packs, task dispatch tables, and import order are outside every typed route preimage.
Repairing outer hashes, copied verdict fields, reused names, stale artifacts, exception text, or successful serialization cannot create routing or authority.
raises: Ordinary wrong types, malformed or noncanonical bytes, missing/surplus objects, conflicts, stale state, unsupported requirements, dependency failures, ambiguity, and deterministic exhaustion return the corresponding closed ordinary result.
